conviction_note: The quarter itself probably lands in the upper half of the company's own $55-60m range: Q1 came in at the top of its range and Q2 above it, and management claimed more than 80% visibility. But this stock has paid little for beats (+2.5% after Q1, +0.3% after Q2), so the move turns on the first Q4 guide. Management's own 'H2 about 15% above H1' framing puts the Q4 bar near $62m, and Gildan said on Nov 5 that blank-apparel demand has slowed since July and stays soft into Q4. Gildan's blanks reach the same screen printers and decorators who buy about 60% of Kornit's systems. The findings sum to -1.0 and the scaled number is -0.26 (p_up 48 x abs 6.5). The gap is small: Gildan is a proxy, Kornit has guided conservatively, and net cash of roughly 60% of market cap with a ~$60m buyback remaining caps the downside, so p_up stays near 50.

That $62m is the street's FY $223.8m and management's own 'H2 ~15% above H1', and it has to hold against Gildan's report of slowing decorator demand.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q4 2026 about $62.4m implied: FY street $223.77m (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krnt/forecast/) less H1 actual $103.9m less Q3 at ~$57.5m. No direct quarterly figure was found.
next_guide.company_current_guide: No Q4 guide yet. On the Q2 call (2026-08-12) the CFO said H2 revenue would be about 15% above H1, supporting high-single-digit FY growth, which implies H2 of ~$119.5m and Q4 ~$62m at the Q3 midpoint (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000).
next_guide.basis: Management set the H2 frame itself, and its habit is to guide conservatively (two straight quarters landed at or above the top of the range), so the base case is a Q4 range bracketing ~$60-64m. Gildan's Nov 5 cut, which says softness persists into Q4, and Cimpress/Vistaprint's miss lean the risk toward a midpoint below $62m rather than above it.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue likely lands in the top half of the company's $55-60m guide, around $58.5-60m against the guide midpoint of $57.5m and street estimates of $57.5-58.6m. Q1 printed $48.5m at the top of a $45-49m guide, Q2 printed $55.3m above a $51-55m guide, and on the Q2 call management claimed 'very good visibility to more than 80% of our revenue' with ARR up $7m in the quarter to $33.8m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 above-top beat with EPS +$0.04 against -$0.02 consensus: +0.34% on the day. Q1 2026 top-of-guide: +2.49%. Q3 2025 EPS beat ($0.09 against $0.02) with in-line revenue: -6.2% on a weak Q4 guide (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). This name does not pay for revenue beats inside its own range.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The street already sits at or above the midpoint ($57.5-58.6m), and the stock bought only +0.3% for the last above-top beat. What is not fully in the bar is a print at or above $60m (the top of the range), which would show the AIC/consumables ramp running ahead of the frame. The beat falls inside the company's own guided range.
findings.independence: The Q1 pattern comes from a separate release (https://marketchameleon.com/PressReleases/i/2304745/KRNT/kornit-digital-reports-first-quarter-2026-results). The visibility quote is from the Q2 call transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000), the same event as the release.

findings.finding: Gildan, the largest supplier of blank T-shirts and fleece to US screen printers and decorators, reported on 2026-11-05 Q3 sales of $1.47bn against its own ~$1.65bn guide. Wholesale fell 10.8% against pro forma, blamed on 'lower replenishment orders from distributors'. Gildan cut FY revenue to $5.4-5.5bn from $6.0-6.2bn, withdrew its 2026-28 targets, said 'the demand recovery we had anticipated has not materialized', and assumes the softness persists into Q4. Kornit's Q3 guide and H2 frame were set on 08-12, before Gildan says conditions changed (after 07-30).
findings.link: The same end customers. Kornit says about 60% of its Q2/H1 system sales went to traditional screen printers, who decorate blanks Gildan sells through distributors (S&S, SanMar). Kornit's ink/AIC revenue scales with the impressions those decorators print. Gildan supplies the input; Kornit supplies the press and consumables. No revenue figure links the two directly.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On the Q4 guide: Q3 2025's guide implied a YoY decline and the stock fell -6.2% despite an EPS beat. Q4 2025's results and 2026 outlook drew +20.65% (baseline; https://www.rttnews.com/3620402/kornit-digital-stock-jumps-20-after-strong-q4-full-year-2025-results.aspx reports +20%). The guide line has produced this name's largest moves.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. KRNT fell -3.4% on 11-05 while IWM fell -4.6%, so it did not react specifically to Gildan. Since 11-09 it is down 6.8% against IWM's 4.5%. Kornit has said nothing since 08-12, and the street FY figure ($223.8m, updated 10-02) still equals management's August H2 frame. If the market had priced Gildan through to Kornit, FY estimates would have come down and the stock would have lagged small caps more than ~1-2 points.
findings.independence: The Kornit CEO said on the Q2 call 'On the long tail, we see customers declining' (https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000). An ASI report from PRINTING United (2026-09-25) cites rising price sensitivity in decorated apparel (https://members.asicentral.com/news/strategy/september-2026/printing-united-expo-2026-print-promo-leaders-take-stock/). Offsetting: Kornit's growth is in strategic accounts and AIC consumables, so it is net of a weak long tail. This is a proxy; Kornit has not confirmed it.

findings.finding: Cimpress reported fiscal Q1 2027 (Sep quarter) on 2026-10-29: revenue +8% but organic constant-currency only +2%, Vistaprint +2% to $464m and the largest gap against Cimpress's own plan, and adj. EBITDA -9%. FY27 targets were held through cost cuts.
findings.link: Vistaprint, Cimpress's largest unit, runs Kornit Apollo systems for apparel ('VistaPrint has significantly increased its apparel production capacity through the implementation of the Kornit Apollo system', per Kornit search results). Kornit gives no revenue share; Vistaprint's apparel is a small part of its $464m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No Cimpress read-through has a recorded KRNT reaction. On guidance generally, see the Gildan finding.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and indirect. No Vistaprint apparel figure was disclosed, so the transmission to Kornit's impressions is inference. KRNT rose from 17.44 (11-02) to 17.87 (11-09) after it, so it was not traded on.

findings.finding: Management's own words set the Q4 bar: 'H2 revenue about 15% higher than H1', with H1 at $103.9m, implies H2 of ~$119.5m and Q4 of ~$62m at the Q3 midpoint, +5% YoY against Q4 2025's $58.9m. The street FY of $223.8m sits exactly there. Kornit's practice is to guide quarters conservatively (two consecutive top-end or above-top landings), so a first Q4 range whose midpoint sits below $62m is a real possibility even with no deterioration. Last November's Q4 guide implied a YoY decline and the stock fell 6.2%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov 2025: Q4 guide $56-60m (implying a YoY decline) plus 'low single-digit' 2026 growth, -6.2% (https://www.itiger.com/news/1142228974). Feb 2026: FY outlook of return to growth and positive EBITDA, +20.65% (baseline). Q4 guidance is the line that moves this stock.
findings.why_not_priced: The street carries management's August frame unchanged (FY $223.8m, updated 2026-10-02), so a conservatively set Q4 range below ~$62m would read as a cut against consensus even if the company still believes the frame. The fall from the Oct 12 high (-9%) prices some of this, but nothing like the -6% reaction to a guide shortfall last November.
findings.independence: The Gildan finding points the same way on the demand side; this finding is about guiding practice and the arithmetic of the frame, not demand, and shares no document with it. FY street: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/krnt/forecast/

findings.finding: The balance sheet caps the downside and funds capital return. At 2026-06-30, cash, deposits and marketable securities were about $451m with no debt, against a ~$713m market cap (42.97m shares at $16.60), so cash is ~63% of the cap and EV ~$260m. About $60m remains under the current buyback authorization; $37.5m was spent in H1 and ~9.5m shares retired since 2023. A new or enlarged authorization alongside the print is plausible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A new $100m program was announced alongside a CFO transition (https://www-web.itiger.com/news/2584623811, date not confirmed). No clean reaction to a buyback by itself has been isolated.
findings.why_not_priced: The cash is public; what is not is whether a new authorization comes now. A priced buyback expectation would show as a stock that does not trade below the low target with 63% of the cap in cash.
findings.independence: Buyback remaining ~$60m from the Q2 call: https://www.webull.com/news/15429991240320000. Share count from the AGM 6-K: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1625791/000121390026095784/ea0304080-6k_kornit.htm

findings.finding: The shekel weakened ~2.9% against the US dollar during Q3 2026 (Bank of Israel, 2026-11-03), and further to ~3.10/$ after the 10-28 Israeli election. Kornit has a large Israeli-shekel cost base and blamed shekel strength for part of a ~190bp YoY gross-margin hit in Q1 2026, so the move is a sequential tailwind to Q3/Q4 margins against guidance set in August.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no isolated FX reaction; margins have mattered through EBITDA guide ranges.
findings.why_not_priced: It is small and a macro-to-company transmission (YoY the shekel is still much stronger than Q3 2025, so it is a sequential help, not a YoY one). Sell-side estimates were last updated 10-02, mostly before the late-quarter weakening.
findings.independence: Q1 2026 FX margin effect: search summary of the Q1 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/05/13/kornit-krnt-q1-2026-earnings-transcript/). The post-election move is from a snippet (https://tradingeconomics.com/israel/currency/news/595811).

findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 printed with the refund and the stock moved +0.3%. No separate reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: It is disclosed; the only question is whether a margin optic disappoints the sequential comparison. Small, and below the guide line.

baseline_tension: There is no option skew and the baseline's reaction history is unreliable. The rebuilt earnings history (-6.2, +20.7, +2.5, +0.3) says the guide line moves the stock and beats do not. The 5-day and 20-day underperformance lines up with my mildly negative guide lean, so part of it is likely already priced.
lessons_applied: Lessons 1 and 6 (verified fact not a reaction; finding inside the company's guided range): the Q3 beat finding cut from +0.8 to +0.4, because the stock bought +0.3% and +2.5% for the last two beats and the expected landing is inside the $55-60m guide.
Lesson 5 (proxy and macro-to-company transmission smaller, not dropped): Gildan cut from -1.5 to -1.2 and Cimpress from -0.4 to -0.3; both kept as filed counterparty proxies.
Lesson 2 (one-offs as one-offs): tariff-refund margin optics cut from -0.2 to -0.1.
Lesson 8 (thin coverage, understatement) and the rebuilt FPI history: abs_move raised from 6.0 to 6.5; p_up moved from 47 to 48 because several caveats point toward 50.
Lesson 7: short interest checked (1.7% of shares, 2.4 DTC); no squeeze adjustment needed. The next-guide (-0.8), expectations, capital and FX findings were left unchanged.
